title: Staged Horizon: Traffic Governor for Canary and Shadow Policy Orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a robust, expressive, and safe policy engine for staged model rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) that integrates with Redwood's serving runtime and Console. Current ad-hoc rollout tooling lacks capacity-awareness, deterministic bucketing, and automatic rollback guardrails tied to both infra metrics (latency/500s) and quality regressions (evaluation harness).

Goals:
- Provide a declarative rollout DSL for traffic splits, step schedules, region-aware routing, and shadowing rules.
- Implement runtime enforcement (control-plane reconciler + runtime hook) that performs capacity-aware stepping and safe auto-rollback.
- Support canary timers, manual pauses, and programmatic aborts; surface decisions in Console with fine-grained telemetry.
- Ensure deterministic bucketing for consistent user assignment across variants and safe A/B measurement windows.
- Make guardrails configurable: SLO thresholds, quality delta on evaluation sets, burst rate protections, and cost limits.

Deliverables:
1) Rollout DSL schema + OpenAPI for CRUD endpoints.
2) Control-plane reconciler service that compiles DSL into runtime route actions (weights, shadow rules).
3) Safety engine that watches metrics and triggers pause/rollback actions with audit trail.
4) Console integration for audit log, timeline, and one-click rollback.

Non-goals: full experimentation analysis (statistical significance) — this ticket focuses on safe rollout orchestration and instrumentation for downstream analysis services.
updates: 2026-01-15: Spike completed. Evaluated existing rollout patterns (percent-step, time-based, metric-based). Decided on a hybrid step scheduler: step can be defined as percent or token-volume and can be conditional on SLOs.

2026-01-22: Architecture decision record (ADR) drafted. Chosen enforcement model: control-plane emits intent; runtime executes fine-grained traffic-split with a short TTL and reports reconciliation status. This reduces blast radius and supports fast rollbacks.

2026-02-03: Design review with PM and Design. PM requested minimum canary floor of 1% and explicit budget caps for cost-sensitive customers. Design asked for timeline UI hooks (start/pause/abort buttons) and events for each step.

2026-02-18: Prototype reconciler implemented (internal branch). Uses consistent-hash bucketing for deterministic A/B assignment and supports region-scoped routing keys. Initial integration tests against local runtime show correct split enforcement and shadow forwarding to a separate telemetry topic.

2026-02-25: Safety engine prototype added. Guardrails implemented: incremental latency delta (p50, p95), error-rate increase (5xx), and quality drift measured by periodic eval against a small stored prompt set. Automatic rollback path triggers when any critical guardrail breaches sustained for 2 minutes.

2026-03-04: Load tests on staging: step-sizes must be capped by available GPU capacity — introduced capacity-aware step adjustment. Observed a false-positive rollback caused by transient infra spike; added short cooldown window (30s) before automatic rollback execution.

2026-03-10: Preparing PR and runbook. Added audit events schema and console event hooks. Requested security review for shadow traffic storage and PII masking. Targeting runtime-1.22 integration early April for Dedicated customers, hosted rollout later in April after e2e testing.

implementation_notes: DSL sketch: versioned JSON schema with fields: name, targets [{model_id, variant}], steps [{type: percent|tokens, value, min_duration, conditions}], shadow: {enabled, sample_rate, destination}, bucketing_key: user_id|session_id, guardrails: [{metric, operator, threshold, duration, severity}], region_overrides.
Reconciler: will compile DSL to route intents and store state in rollout-store (durable kv). Use optimistic concurrency on rollout ID, serialize transitions, emit audit events to timeline topic.
Runtime hook: short-lived traffic policy with TTL. Runtime reports back observed split and health signals. Use gRPC control channel with ack semantics to avoid drift.
Safety engine: pluggable metric adapters (Prometheus for infra, quality-service for evals). Supports soft alarms (pause) and hard alarms (rollback). Cooldown/backoff to avoid oscillation.
Testing: synthetic traffic harness to exercise token-volume steps and shadow logging. Add mutation tests to simulate partial failures of runtime node to ensure rollback still executes.
Console: expose start/pause/abort actions and an audit timeline with reason codes. Add suggested remediation steps for common rollback reasons (increase capacity, revert model, reduce prompt size).
Telemetry: emit events: rollout.created, step.started, step.succeeded, step.paused, step.rolled_back, rollback.executed, audit.note — include correlation IDs for traces.
